config.note: LM Studio headless (llmster 0.0.25-1) with its newest MLX runtime 1.13.1, set up as a fan would: LM Studio's staff pick qwen/qwen3.8-27b (hub model.yaml revision 4), whose Mac variant is lmstudio-community/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit @6067b15c, which is exactly our trunk (~/.nace/models/qwen3.8-27b-4bit, the files Kapitsa/mlx-lm/MTPLX read; the mtp.safetensors sidecar is not part of it), linked file by file. `lms load qwen/qwen3.8-27b --context-length 32768 --parallel 1`. Everything else is LM Studio's default. The MLX engine runs these vision checkpoints through its batched mlx-vlm path (BatchedVisionModelKit), which offers no speculative decoding: a draft model is refused ('not supported for batched vision models'; mlx-lm's draft speculation would also need trimmable caches, which the GatedDeltaNet layers' ArraysCache is not), mlx-vlm drops mtp.* weights (LM Studio's --speculative-draft-mtp is a llama.cpp/GGUF feature), and KV-cache quantization is not available on that path. Prompt cache: RAM plus LM Studio's default disk tier (unlinked temp file in /tmp). Thinking is switched off per request by reasoning_effort none, which LM Studio maps to the hub model's enableThinking custom field (chat_template_kwargs is ignored; without the hub model.yaml neither works). Usage is reported in the stream; cached prompt tokens are not. LM Studio stops at max_tokens-1 (511 of 512, checked by re-tokenizing the text), so every decode run carries a completion_tokens flag; rates use the reported count. Daemon pid from ~/.lmstudio/.internal/llmster-pid.lock: memory is the whole llmster tree (daemon + node worker hosting the engine). GGUF route: LM Studio's own lmstudio-community Q4_K_M GGUF (16.8 GB) does carry the MTP layer (blk.64.nextn) and the llama.cpp runtime 2.60.0 (b11698) can draft with it (--speculative-draft-mtp); it was not measured inside LM Studio because the 16.8 GB download no longer fit the 10 GB disk reserve while other jobs were writing (free fell 31 -> 25 GB during its first 2 GB; aborted and deleted). Standalone llama.cpp b11669 on the same quant: MTP n-max 3 18.3 tok/s (plain 10.0), prefill 84/77 tok/s, 30.6 GB peak.
